knowledge_gain: If only cross-referential distance causes the memory/no-memory crossover, long-horizon is an ill-posed target; if no factor crosses, the no-memory advantage is structural under current baselines.
decision_changed: Memory/context teams would target specific task factors instead of treating long-horizon as a coherent regime.
reason: Factorial design cleanly separates horizon properties that existing work (2604.11978, 2606.24775) conflates.

knowledge_gain: If oracle memory leaves attributed planning/instruction failures unchanged, memory misses are causally irrelevant to planning-dominant taxonomies; if failures shift, those taxonomies overstate planning and understate memory.
decision_changed: Failure-attribution tools would add memory-oracle counterfactuals before quoting planning-dominant shares as evidence against memory investment.
reason: Adds the missing causal counterfactual to attribution work; TRAJDEBUG/Seeing the Whole Elephant do not inject oracle memory.

knowledge_gain: If stepwise reminders erase instruction errors, the deficit is attention/context, not storage; if the memory system is necessary, storage remains involved.
decision_changed: Memory-architecture pitches would have to distinguish storage deficits from attention deficits before claiming the agent forgot instructions.
reason: Cheap reminder baseline cleanly separates storage from attention; Memory-R2/FLARE lack this ablation.

knowledge_gain: If stronger planning does not make memory-error share dominant, memory is not automatically the next bottleneck; if it does, the planning-dominant attribution is planner-dependent.
decision_changed: Agenda setters would prioritize memory based on planner strength rather than current failure shares.
reason: Planner-strength control addresses a hidden variable in 2604.11978's attribution conclusion.

knowledge_gain: If random truncation matches learned selective memory, learned selection is not the active ingredient; if learned matches oracle summary, the active ingredient is placing right items in context, not the memory mechanism.
decision_changed: Selective-memory papers would report random-truncation and oracle-summary arms before claiming learned-policy value.
reason: Three-arm budget test separates information availability from learned selection; MemDelta only partially overlaps.

knowledge_gain: As framed it only separates recall from downstream action; with state-update scoring it would reveal whether correct recall fails during state update or action selection.
decision_changed: Retrieval benchmarks would report recall-to-state-to-action checkpoints instead of memory EM as a standalone proxy.
reason: The minimal test omits explicit state-update scoring, so the three-way decomposition is not actually falsified.
pivot_to: Score recall-to-state-update-to-action transitions to separate state update from action selection.

knowledge_gain: If memory advantage is flat across an interference gradient, multi-target interference is not the trigger for memory intervention; if it grows, memory investment can be justified on interference grounds.
decision_changed: Benchmark designers would stop citing multi-target interference as a generic memory motivation and condition on interference level.
reason: Useful moderation but close to MINTEval's existing gradient; risk of collapse into adaptation.

knowledge_gain: If one intervention cluster dominates at equal cost, allocation gets an empirical effect-size ordering; if none does, no cluster is privileged under current canonical choices.
decision_changed: Funders and lab leads would switch from cluster-faith prioritization to cost-matched effect sizes.
reason: Decision-relevant but likely collapses into representative-dependent bake-off; not mechanism-revealing.
